oneLine: Plans moving stock between warehouses: advises, then runs an approved transfer from stock reservation through pick, dispatch and arrival.

rows.title: Keep the site capability copy
rows.story: facility-layout says which sites may send or receive transfers. Here a local copy follows it, and a newer revision replaces the older one, so planning never has to ask.
rows.policy: Whenever a site's capability changes, replace its row if the revision is newer

rows.title: Keep the demand copy
rows.story: order-management reports the units each order line needs from a site. A local copy keeps the newest fact per line. A removed line counts for nothing.
rows.policy: Whenever an order line's demand changes, keep its newest version; a removed line counts for none

rows.title: Keep the capacity plan copy
rows.story: warehouse-planning publishes capacity plans. A local copy keeps the newest plan for each plan id. A plan with no site is left out.
rows.policy: Whenever a plan for a site is published, keep the newest version of it

rows.title: Set the rebalance rules
rows.story: An operator writes the policies that say which SKUs may move, and the lanes between sites. The scheduled rebalance plans only from these catalogues. Lanes are set the same way.

rows.title: Try out transfers without committing
rows.story: An operator submits positions, policies and lanes and gets advisory proposals back. A simulation can instead use the local copies. Nothing is reserved or published.

rows.title: Approve a transfer and ask for stock
rows.story: An operator approves a proposal. It is checked against the local copies, and refused if a fact is missing or stale. SKUs sold in cases move in whole cases. inventory-storage is then asked for the origin stock.

then.does: reserves the origin stock and answers allocated or rejected

rows.title: Release the pick once stock is held
rows.story: inventory-storage reports the stock reserved. The transfer becomes allocated and the pick work is released in the same step, so an allocated transfer never lacks its pick work.
rows.policy: Whenever origin stock is reserved, mark the transfer allocated and release its pick work

then.does: creates the transfer pick as a work unit referring to the transfer

rows.title: Give up when stock cannot be held
rows.story: inventory-storage refuses the reservation, with a reason from a fixed list. The transfer is marked unfulfillable and ends there.
rows.policy: Whenever origin stock cannot be reserved, mark the transfer unfulfillable with the reason

rows.title: Cancel a transfer
rows.story: An operator cancels with a reason. Before any stock is held the transfer is cancelled at once. If stock is already reserved, a release is requested first. From picking onwards the cancel is refused.

then.does: lets go of the origin reservation and reports back

rows.title: Finish a cancel once the hold is gone
rows.story: inventory-storage confirms the origin reservation is released, or was already gone. Either way the hold no longer exists, so the transfer is cancelled for good.
rows.policy: Whenever the origin reservation is released, mark the cancelling transfer cancelled

rows.title: Release the dispatch once picked
rows.story: fulfillment-execution reports the pick, possibly short. The picked quantity is recorded and dispatch work is released for exactly that quantity.
rows.policy: Whenever the pick completes, record the picked quantity and release the dispatch work

then.does: creates the dispatch as a work unit referring to the transfer

rows.title: Mark the transfer in transit
rows.story: fulfillment-execution reports that the goods left the origin. The transfer moves to in transit. No work is released for this step.
rows.policy: Whenever dispatch completes, mark the transfer in transit

rows.title: Mark the transfer arrived
rows.story: inventory-storage reports the receipt staged at the destination. A work-driven arrival fact from fulfillment-execution may also exist. Whichever comes first moves the transfer to arrived; the other is skipped.
rows.policy: Whenever the first arrival signal comes, mark the transfer arrived

rows.title: Close the transfer once stowed
rows.story: inventory-storage reports the goods stowed at the destination, with where they went. The transfer is received and its journey ends.
rows.policy: Whenever the stow is confirmed, mark the transfer received and keep where the stock went

rows.title: Flag transfers that are stuck
rows.story: A periodic check compares each open transfer with a time limit for its state and reports the ones past it. It only reports: it never cancels or changes a transfer.
rows.policy: Every check, report each open transfer that has stayed too long in its state

rows.title: Run a scheduled rebalance
rows.story: On a schedule, the planner works from the local copies and the operator's catalogues, and records how many proposals it made and how many it rejected. It never approves anything.
rows.policy: Every run, plan proposals from the local copies and record the outcome, without approving any

hotspots.text: A transfer can no longer be cancelled once picking has started. The stock is moving, and there is no damage or short-pick flow yet.
If the dispatch path is not configured, the dispatch work is withheld and nothing releases it later. The transfer waits in picked.
The scheduled rebalance cannot see stock positions, so it plans only from site capability, demand and catalogues.
The stuck-transfer check only reports. Nothing retries or recovers a stuck transfer on its own.
The dwell report shows a transfer's age at each step, not the time spent in a state. A true dwell time needs a new field.

opportunities.text: If a sibling context ever publishes stock positions, they could be kept locally and the scheduled pass could plan from real stock.
Adding a dwell-seconds field to the state-change event would give a true time-in-state report.
